result.markdown: --- title: "02 · Simple regression" subtitle: "Week 1" --- ::: {.guiding-q} How does one variable predict another? ::: ## In this session - Least squares: fitting a line with `lm()` - Interpreting intercept, slope and residual standard deviation - Inference: standard errors, confidence intervals, *t*- and *p*-values - Assumptions and diagnostics: residual plots, influential cases - Reporting a regression result ::: {.key-terms} **Key terms:** [Intercept](../../glossary.qmd#intercept), [Residuals](../../glossary.qmd#residuals), [Standard error](../../glossary.qmd#standard-error), [Confidence interval](../../glossary.qmd#confidence-interval), [*p*-value](../../glossary.qmd#p-value), [Assumptions (of the linear model)](../../glossary.qmd#assumptions), [Heteroscedasticity](../../glossary.qmd#heteroscedasticity), [Influential cases](../../glossary.qmd#influential-cases), [Cook's distance](../../glossary.qmd#cooks-distance) ::: ## Learning goals After this session you can - fit a simple regression in R and interpret its coefficients, - explain what a standard error and a confidence interval mean, - check model assumptions with diagnostic plots. ## Simulate first If we simulate data from a known model again and again, the estimated slopes scatter around the true value. Their spread *is* the standard error. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(2) true_b1 <- 0.8 slopes <- replicate(2000, { age <- runif(30, 1, 10) mass <- 3 + true_b1 * age + rnorm(30, 0, 1.5) coef(lm(mass ~ age))[2] }) hist(slopes, breaks = 40, col = "#1b6f8a", border = "white", main = "Sampling distribution of the slope", xlab = "Estimated slope") abline(v = true_b1, col = "#c0392b", lwd = 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-simple-regression_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=975} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} sd(slopes) # compare with the SE that summary(lm(...)) reports for one sample ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> [1] 0.1070556 ``` ::: ::: ## Materials ::: {.materials} - Slides coming soon - R script coming soon - Exercises coming soon ::: ## Reading - Gelman, Hill & Vehtari (2020), ch. 6–7. - Fox, J. (2016). *Applied regression analysis and generalized linear models* (3rd ed.), ch. 5–6. Sage.
